## Why This Benchmark Is Included

Diffusion is a major iterative generative-model workload class.

| **Field** | **Value** |
|:---|:---|
| **Classroom value** | Exposes iterative denoising, precision behavior, scheduler design, and generative quality evaluation. |
| **Systems behavior** | Repeated UNet execution, scheduler overhead, and precision sensitivity. |
| **Benchmark lineage** | The authors publish the paper, reference code, checkpoint, sampler, reference statistics, and exact FID procedure. |
| **Model choice** | The 55.7-million-parameter official checkpoint is small enough for local inference and has a stronger published baseline than the earlier Google DDPM candidate. |
| **Dataset choice** | CIFAR-10 and its reference statistics are fixed by the upstream checkpoint and evaluator. |
| **Quality metric** | Upstream requires exactly 50,000 generated images for FID and rejects smaller sets. |
| **Published baseline** | 1.79 FID using the official 18-step deterministic sampler and 35 network evaluations per image |
| **Alternative rejected** | A custom MNIST diffusion trainer, reduced FID set, or denoising-only metric has no equivalent quality contract. |

## Authoritative Sources and Adaptation

| **Field** | **Value** |
|:---|:---|
| **Authority** | NVIDIA EDM reference implementation |
| **Repository** | [open source](https://github.com/NVlabs/edm) |
| **Commit** | `008a4e5316c8e3bfe61a62f874bddba254295afb` |

**Adaptation boundary:** The max runner uses the exact NVIDIA three-trial seed stream and 18-step sampler, retains sampler state in float64 on CPU while using float32 Apple MPS network evaluations, generates 50,000 images per trial, and applies the byte-pinned official Inception FID evaluator.

## How to Run

```bash
# one-time asset preparation
uv run mlperf fetch --workload image-generation --profile max

# benchmark run (writes JSON/HTML/CSV reports + .provd.json provenance)
uv run mlperf run --workload image-generation --profile max

# quick smoke pass
uv run mlperf run --workload image-generation --profile min

# research envelope
uv run mlperf run --workload image-generation --profile pro
```

See the [running guide](../../guide/running.qmd) for profile semantics, report handling, and power measurement flags.

## Candidate Quality Target

| **Field** | **Value** |
|:---|:---|
| **Metric** | fid |
| **Target** | 1.79 |
| **Direction** | lower |
| **Target kind** | published reference reproduction |
| **Target basis** | literature |
| **Tolerance** | 0.0 |
| **Reference runs** | 3 |

**Reviewer notes:**

- The target is the published NVIDIA EDM CIFAR-10 minimum FID across three independent 50,000-image trials using the official deterministic sampler.
- One MLPerf EDU acceptance run is one three-trial result packet. The three trials are part of the upstream score definition, not optional timing repetitions.
- The max runner binds the checkpoint, source, Inception detector, reference statistics, seed ranges 0-49999, 50000-99999, and 100000-149999, and the official FID calculation.
- The provenance-bound Apple MPS packet rescored all three retained 50,000-image sets and reproduced a minimum FID of 1.8015540749997014; the target and tolerance remain unchanged.

## Results

Run the benchmark and read your own report:

```bash
uv run mlperf run --workload image-generation --profile max
```

Every run writes an HTML dashboard for reading, JSON for machine use, CSV for spreadsheets, and a `.provd.json` provenance manifest. Those artifacts carry the quality decision, timing distribution, hardware and software fingerprint, asset digests, and model lineage for the run you performed.

See [Reading Results](../../guide/results.qmd) for how to interpret them.
